svg.aria-label: An IPv6-only phone reaching an IPv4-only server through DNS64, which synthesizes an address, and a NAT64 translator

text.class: mid mono xs b f-green halo

g.text: It only has an IPv4 address, 203.0.113.80,
so the name server makes up an IPv6 one:

ol.li: Many mobile networks now give phones only IPv6. When Alice’s phone looks up a website that only has an IPv4 address, it asks for an IPv6 address (an AAAA record, Chapter 29), as usual.
The provider’s name server finds no AAAA record, so it makes one up: the IPv4 address, written in hex, on the end of a special prefix, 64:ff9b::/96. This is DNS64.

Packets to that prefix are routed to a NAT64 translator, which rewrites them as IPv4 packets from one of its own IPv4 addresses, like Chapter 22’s NAT, and translates the answers back. The phone never knew.

figure.figcaption: DNS64 and NAT64: how an IPv6-only phone reaches the IPv4 internet.
